insights.title: Pay off your $12,114 credit card to stop $3,028/yr in interest
insights.description: Your credit card carries a 24.99% APR on a $12,114 balance, costing roughly $3,028 in interest each year. Your checking account holds $42,880, more than enough to clear this in full today. Transfer $12,114 from Account 5 to the credit card and eliminate the highest-rate debt you carry.
insights.chatPrompt: Should I pay off my credit card with my checking account balance?

insights.title: Boost retirement savings to $11,100/mo to reach $6.25M by age 58, not 2045
insights.description: Goal 3 is projected to complete in November 2045, but your target retirement age is 58, which is roughly 2038. That is a 7-year gap. Starting from your current $1,477,135 balance and assuming 7% annual growth, you need roughly $11,100/mo in total contributions to hit $6.25M by 2038. At your current pace you are contributing closer to $2,000/mo toward this goal. Increase your combined 401k, Roth 401k, and brokerage contributions by approximately $9,100/mo to close the gap.
insights.chatPrompt: How much more do I need to save each month to retire at 58 with $6.25 million?

insights.title: Roll your $123,213 IRA into your 401(k), then contribute $7,000 via backdoor Roth
insights.description: At your income level as a married couple, you are above the direct Roth IRA contribution limit, so the backdoor Roth (contribute to a nondeductible traditional IRA then convert to Roth) is the correct route. However, your $123,213 traditional IRA balance triggers the pro-rata rule, making most of any conversion taxable now. The standard fix is to roll the entire traditional IRA into your 401k (Account 3 accepts IRA rollovers in most plans), which zeroes out the pre-tax balance and lets you convert a clean $7,000 nondeductible contribution with no pro-rata drag. Confirm your 401k plan allows incoming IRA rollovers and verify the strategy with a tax professional before executing.
insights.chatPrompt: How do I do a backdoor Roth when I already have a traditional IRA?

insights.title: Add international funds to lift your portfolio from 11% to 30% international
insights.description: Your VXUS holdings total roughly $96,052 against approximately $853,000 in total fund and equity holdings, putting international exposure at about 11%. The broadly used benchmark for a moderate-risk portfolio is 30 to 40% international. At your current allocation you are heavily concentrated in US equities, which adds home-country risk. Direct new brokerage contributions into VXUS or a similar international fund until it reaches roughly $255,000 (30% of your current holdings base), and redirect a portion of future VOO or VTI purchases to close the gap over the next 12 months.
insights.chatPrompt: How overweight US equities am I and how should I rebalance toward international?

insights.title: Invest $68,234 of idle cash to earn about $2,047/yr more
insights.description: Your depository accounts total $193,232 against six months of monthly income at $124,998, leaving $68,234 sitting in checking and savings beyond a comfortable emergency cushion. At a 3% spread between cash yields and expected long-term market returns, that excess costs you roughly $2,047 per year in foregone growth. Move $68,234 from Account 13 or Account 12 into Account 10 (taxable brokerage) and invest it in your existing index fund mix.
insights.chatPrompt: How much of my cash savings should I move into investments?

insights.title: Max your HSA at $8,550/yr and keep it invested for retirement
insights.description: You already hold $31,728 in your HSA (Account 9) and it is invested in equities, which is excellent. The 2026 family HSA limit is $8,550 and contributions are deductible, grow tax-free, and come out tax-free for qualified medical expenses in retirement. If you are not already contributing the full $8,550 this year, increase your payroll HSA election to hit that ceiling. The HSA functions as a stealth retirement account for healthcare costs after 65, and every dollar invested now compounds without drag.
insights.chatPrompt: Am I getting the most out of my HSA as a retirement savings tool?

insights.title: Pay off your $27,360 auto loan for a guaranteed 7.4% return
insights.description: Your auto loan carries a 7.4% interest rate on a $27,360 balance. Paying it off early is equivalent to earning a guaranteed 7.4% after-tax return, which is difficult to beat on a risk-adjusted basis with a taxable account. After clearing the credit card (Step 3 above), direct excess cash from Account 13 toward this loan. Eliminating it frees up your monthly auto payment for additional retirement or brokerage contributions.
insights.chatPrompt: Should I pay off my auto loan early or keep the money invested?
